# Maintenance Reminders (MR V2) — exhaustive design drive, 2026-10-06

**Package:** `build/maintenance-reminder-v2/sources/design-MR_V2_2-2026-10-06/` (export of the Claude Design project "MR V2", taken 2026-10-06).  
**Driver (generic, reusable):** `build/testing-tools/drive_design_full.py` · **this report is generated by** `analyze_drive.py` in this folder (section 3 is hand-written: `spec-comparison.md`).  
**Not written:** TestRail, Jira, git — nothing was committed or pushed.

## Summary

- Boards driven: **9 of 9** (the 6 boards in `design_handoff_maintenance_reminders/` are byte-identical copies, 1e). Pages reached by the board's own navigation and by URL hash / scrolling: all (1c).
- Interactive/responsive elements found: **6801**; hovered **6801**, clicked **6801**; covered by a drawn overlay and driven again with forced hover + forced click: **1819**. Interactions recorded: **17240**; exposed something: **1334** (tooltips / hover cards **840**, native title tooltips **301**, opened another board **193**), plus **2335** clicks that followed an in-board arrow to another artboard; failed: **0**; missing: **0** → **100%**.
- Hidden text blocks revealed by an interaction: **418 of 418**.
- Comparison with the current spec (section 3): **63** design-only details a tester would see (3a); **28** design-differs-from-spec items (3b), plus **7** spec states no artboard draws and 2 navigation dead ends.

## 0 · How the design was driven

- Every board loaded from INSIDE the package folder over `file://` with Chromium's `--allow-file-access-from-files`, so the dc runtime can fetch the sibling component boards (ShopviewHeader, SettingsSidebar) that draw the app chrome. React 18.3.1, ReactDOM and Babel (which `support.js` pulls from unpkg) were fetched with verified TLS through the agent proxy's CA bundle and handed to the browser; nothing was disabled.
- Pages reached through each board's OWN navigation: the header page pills (Chunk 1: `1 Settings`, `2 The asset`, `3 Customers`; Chunk 2: `4 Work order`, `5 Estimation & email`) were clicked AND each page was loaded by URL hash; `All chunks`, `Chunk 1`/`Chunk 2` and every other cross-board link was followed and its landing checked. Boards with no page navigation (Demo, Canned lines proposal, 4-work-order, Flow map) have no ids on their sections: each top-level section is a page reached by scrolling the canvas.
- Every interactive or responsive element was enumerated (button, a, ARIA roles, inputs/selects/textarea, summary/details, `[onclick]`/`data-*` actions, `[tabindex]`, tooltip hosts `.sv-tt-host`/`[title]`/`[aria-describedby]`, hosts of every CSS `:hover`/`:focus-within` reveal rule, React handlers, and every element whose computed cursor is pointer — the outermost pointer element AND every descendant that only inherits the pointer cursor, the latter driven with a 250 ms wait instead of 500 ms). No cap.
- Each element: scrolled into view from a fresh known state (board reloaded whenever the previous interaction changed the DOM or the document; otherwise pointer parked on empty canvas, focus cleared and the board's own page hash re-navigated), then HOVERED with the real mouse and, separately, CLICKED with the real mouse; newly visible text, navigation, focus, style change and occlusion recorded; a screenshot whenever something new appeared.
- **Elements covered by an overlay drawn over the screen** (a modal or hover card drawn on top of the artboard) cannot be reached by a real pointer. Every such element was driven AGAIN with `:hover`/`:focus-within` FORCED through the DevTools protocol on it and all its ancestors ("forced hover"), and activated with its own click event ("forced click").
- JS census (DevTools `getEventListeners` on every element + React props): the boards carry NO click/hover handlers of their own — the only listeners are React's delegated root and image load/error. All behaviour is links (in-board arrows and cross-board links) and CSS hover/focus reveals (tooltips, hover cards). There are no `<select>`, `<input>`, `<details>` elements: dropdowns, menus and dialogs are DRAWN open on their own artboards, so their options are in the page texts (`<board>-pages.txt`).
- **Proof of completeness for hidden content:** before driving, every hidden text block on each board (opacity 0 / visibility hidden / display none) was inventoried; the run then proves which interaction revealed each one (table 1b).
- Variants: each board re-rendered in dark theme (`?theme=dark`) and at 768 px and 1920 px widths; component boards rendered with every declared prop value (ShopviewHeader `nav` = customers / workOrders / schedule / none; SettingsSidebar `active` = maintenance / none), including the two values no board uses.

## 2 · Everything exposed by interaction (verbatim), by board, page and story

Grouped and de-duplicated: one line per distinct text per artboard. `where` = on the product screen, or a designer note on the artboard caption. `how` = hover / click (real pointer) / forced (element covered by an overlay drawn over the screen). Screenshots: `screenshots/`. Dropdown/menu/dialog options are drawn open on their own artboards (no live dropdowns exist) — they are in `<board>-pages.txt`. Link navigation (in-board arrows and cross-board links) is summarised at the end of each board.

**Page `page1` 1Settings**

- *S2 Add a routine service*

## 3 · Comparison against the CURRENT specification

Specification used (the authority for expected behaviour):
- Chunk 1 — `sources/CONFLUENCE-886931488-Chunk1-MR-2026-10-06.md` (Confluence page 886931488, read 2026-10-06)
- Chunk 2 — `sources/CONFLUENCE-897679389-Chunk2-MR-2026-10-06.md` (Confluence page 897679389, read 2026-10-06)

Method: every text the drive EXPOSED (tooltips, hover cards, native title tooltips, designer notes) was matched
sentence-by-sentence against both specs (scripted shortlist, then read by hand); in addition the screens' visible
labels were checked for ~90 UI strings the spec states (button names, headings, empty states, messages, toasts).
"Designer note" = a hover on the artboard caption (the board's annotation, not part of the product screen).
The design gives screen names, navigation and what a tester sees; where it disagrees with the spec, **the spec wins**.

### 3a · Design-only details a tester would see (the spec does not state this text)

Each item: story · where (board / artboard) · how it is reached · the exposed text verbatim · note.

**Navigation dead ends found by clicking every link** (a tester following the design will hit these):
- Chunk 1 → 35 "Create work order" links point to `Chunk 2.dc.html#v5`; Chunk 2 has no `v5` artboard, so they land on the top of Chunk 2 (the other 4 targets, `#wo1` ×7 and `#i1` ×2, exist).
- 4-work-order (old WO chrome) → 54 links point to `1-settings-schedules.dc.html`, `2-asset-maintenance.dc.html`, `3-customers-reminders.dc.html`, `5-estimation-and-email.dc.html` and `all-boards.dc.html` (with `#s3`, `#s4`, `#x1`, `#b1`): none of these files is in the package root (older copies exist only under `_archive-pages/`/`_backup-before-ds/`, authorized not to open), so every one is "file not found". Only its "Maintenance Reminders" link works.

- S1-E2 "A name already in use is refused inline: A schedule with this name already exists." — not drawn (V1 shows other validation messages only).
- S7-E1 "offers Mark as done or Leave due. The default is done" — not drawn.
- S7-R19 count statement on turning notifications off — not drawn (see 3b-15).
- S11-R17 / S11-R26 "No data" state — the words "No data" appear on no artboard.
- S11-R27 "The meter's hover ends with: This is the system's best estimate from this unit's past readings. Check its history if in doubt. Beside it, View work orders opens the asset's Work Orders tab" — not drawn (see 3b-4).
- S13-R33 "With a tile, filter or search active and nothing matching, the table reads No reminders match, with Clear filters" — not drawn.
- S1-R10 "Move up / Move down" — not drawn (see 3b-13).
